facts.fact: The policy centre's analyst Ruaa Taha writes that Sudan has no legal framework regulating personal data given to AI chat systems, and that neither new authority has issued binding rules by mid-2026.
Decrees in November 2025 created the Sudanese Data and AI Authority, a body with a mandate over data and AI, per the article citing the AI Regulation Tracker.

SDN.note: The document states nothing on AI in use in government bodies.

facts.fact: The article says Sudan has no legal framework governing AI chat systems and that the Data and AI Authority created in November 2025 had issued no binding rules by mid-2026.

facts.fact: Decrees in November 2025 created the Sudanese Cybersecurity Authority, per the article citing the AI Regulation Tracker; it had issued no binding rules by mid-2026.
The article states Sudan's Informatics Crimes Law of 2018 replaced the 2007 computer crimes law and was amended in 2020.
The article says banking activity in Sudan runs on foreign-hosted apps without any legal requirement governing data localisation or cross-border transfer.
The article states Sudan has no data protection law: a draft written in 2018 was never enacted.
The article states Sudan has no data protection law in force; a 2018 draft was never enacted.
The article says Sudan is a signatory to the African Union's Malabo Convention but has not domesticated it.
The article says no legal requirement governs cross-border transfer of data in Sudan.
The article says Sudan signed the Malabo Convention and has not yet put it into domestic law.
